claim: Strategy is best described as a pattern in a stream of decisions; realized strategy differs from intended strategy, and the gap is the object of study (deliberate, unrealized, emergent). Two cases only, qualitative.
agent_test: Log intended plan vs executed action trace on long tasks; measure plan-action divergence rate and whether divergences that were kept helped final score.

claim: Deliberate and emergent are ends of a continuum; real strategies mix both (eight types named by Mintzberg and Waters).
agent_test: Compare pure-plan, pure-reactive and mixed scaffold at equal tokens; mixed should dominate on tasks with hidden state.

claim: The planning-versus-learning dispute (Ansoff vs Mintzberg, 1991) was never settled by qualitative cases. Two later meta-analyses find a positive link between planning and performance: George, Walker, Monster (2019) r = .229 [.186,.271] over 87 correlations in 31 studies (I2 = 91.6%); Hamann et al. (2023) 183 samples, larger under high uncertainty (abstract only). Effects are modest, heterogeneous, and smaller in multi-source studies.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as prior that planning helps on average but not for every decision.

claim: Emergent strategies can arise from lower-level initiatives that top management later legitimises (Burgelman Intel; Honda US entry story).
agent_test: Let sub-steps log unplanned successes; test a retro step that promotes them into the plan versus discarding them.

claim: Interleaving reasoning with action (ReAct) beats acting alone: ALFWorld best trial 71% vs Act 45% vs BUTLER 37% (verified).
agent_test: Ablate thoughts between actions at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reactive loops fail through reasoning error and repeated steps: 47% of ReAct failures vs 16% of CoT failures (HotpotQA, 200 sampled; not re-verified).
agent_test: Add a repeat-step detector; measure fall in repeated-action failures.

claim: A reflect-note-retry learning loop gives large gains where feedback is a real check: ALFWorld 130/134 in 12 trials, HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1; no gain with vague feedback or small model; MBPP worse (77.1 vs 80.1).
agent_test: Run retry with and without verbal notes, with and without a hard verifier, at equal total tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Static up-front plans can be worse than reactive execution: WebShop Plan-and-Execute 17.0 vs ReAct 32.0 vs ADaPT 44.0 (GPT-3.5); ALFWorld P&E = ReAct 43.3; TextCraft P&E 27 vs ReAct 19.
agent_test: Same task set, static plan vs as-needed decomposition vs reactive; report per-task-type.

claim: Plan revision beats a fixed plan: dynamic replanning adds +10.31 points over the static planner (43.63 to 53.94) on WebArena-Lite; the proper no-planner baseline is the fine-tuned executor at 36.97, so a static planner adds about 6.7 and replanning about 17. (Original a22 line overstated by using the untuned 9.85.) AdaPlanner (2023) shows the same direction with a plan-prediction mismatch trigger, but no equal-token test of replan-when exists.
agent_test: Replan after every step vs after failure only vs never, equal tokens.

claim: Decomposing as needed, only when the executor fails, beats fixed-depth decomposition: TextCraft depth-3 recipes 38.7 vs ReAct 1.8; depth-2 78.2 vs 26.9.
agent_test: Trigger decomposition on failure only versus always.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Separating planning from observation saves tokens (ReWOO: 64% fewer tokens, +4.4 points over 6 benchmarks) and is more robust to tool failure than ReAct (ReAct accuracy 40.8 to 0, ReWOO 42.4 to 13.2). Both still degrade.
agent_test: Plan-then-execute without re-observing as a cheap mode when tools are reliable.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs alone plan poorly: GPT-4 206/600 (34.3%) on Blocksworld, 4.3% on Mystery Blocksworld, 0.6% TravelPlanner; an external verifier lifts Blocks World to 82% with up to 15 rounds.
agent_test: Add a symbolic or rule checker to plan steps; measure feasibility rate.

claim: Long-horizon business agents drift and collapse: Vending-Bench best model $2,217.93 mean (min $476) vs human $844 (one run); high variance, some runs stop after ~18 days.
agent_test: Run 5+ seeds; report min as well as mean; test memory and periodic re-plan.

claim: Memory and structured state help long-horizon plan-execute agents: EcoGym Gemini-3-Pro none 11282, episodic 18939; longer context gave no consistent gain.
agent_test: Episodic notes vs raw context at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-written business plans are rated slightly above entrepreneurs' plans by investors (+0.14 SD, p<0.001; accept +5 pts p=0.003; interest in intro +3 pts p=0.094 not significant); gain vanishes versus accepted plans; LLM-VC rating correlation 0.52.
agent_test: Not a test of emergent strategy; caution on judging plans by rated quality.

claim: Entrepreneurial planning evidence is mixed and was not opened (Delmar and Shane, Brinckmann meta-analysis small positive, Camuffo, Koning); no firm numbers.
agent_test: Open sources before use.

claim: No published LLM study directly tests deliberate versus emergent strategy; closest are plan-vs-replan agent ablations.
agent_test: Design our own: intended-plan vs realized-trace divergence experiment.

claim: Planning has a small-to-moderate positive average link to performance: r = .229 (95% CI .186-.271, k = 87 correlations, 31 studies) and .255 when averaged per study, strongest for effectiveness and formal planning, weakest for efficiency (-.357). Sector and country do not moderate. Egger test flags possible publication bias.
agent_test: Treat a written plan as worth its cost on average; score it on goal achievement, not on efficiency. Compare plan vs no-plan at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The planning benefit is larger under high environmental uncertainty and for larger firms (Hamann, Halw, Guenther 2023, 183 samples); this runs against the simple reading that plans fail in turbulence. Only the abstract was opened; effect sizes unverified.
agent_test: Test whether an explicit plan helps more on tasks with hidden state or noise (CEO-Bench style) than on stable tasks.

claim: Teaching entrepreneurs to act like scientists (hypothesis, test, pivot) improved performance in a randomised trial of 116 Italian startups and raised pivoting without raising dropout; A/B-testing adoption by startups is linked to more page views and launches and to both faster scaling and faster failure. Direction only; effect sizes not opened.
agent_test: Make each plan step carry a testable hypothesis and a pivot rule; measure pivots and early stops.

claim: Reflection and self-correction help when a hard verifier or true label exists and not otherwise: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5 with oracle labels vs 75.9 to 74.7 intrinsic; CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8 intrinsic. Reflexion and Self-Refine stay below CoT on rubric-judged consulting cases; adding unverified reflections hurt ExpeL.
agent_test: Only write lessons into memory when a checkable outcome supports them; tag lessons verified vs unverified.

claim: Promoting verified successes from execution into a reusable plan or memory helps in text and web tasks: AdaPlanner skill discovery nearly doubles ALFWorld success (+15 on MiniWoB++); AWM +24.6% / +51.1% relative on Mind2Web / WebArena; ExpeL learned insights beat hand-crafted. All have a success signal; no business-strategy test.
agent_test: Promote a pattern into the plan only after repeated verified success; log promoted patterns and test with and without.

claim: LLM agents show plan momentum: they commit early, then do not recover (39% average drop multi-turn vs single-turn, unreliability +112%, 15 models); models that weigh conflicting advice more act less decisively; MAST lists step repetition, unawareness of termination and reasoning-action mismatch as common drift modes. No study yet operationalises an outside-signal break trigger.
agent_test: Trigger: when a new observation contradicts a plan prediction, restart from a recap instead of patching; compare against patching at equal tokens.

claim: 2026 business-simulation benchmarks show large run-to-run and backbone-to-backbone variance: CEO-Bench 3 runs per model with only 3 models above start cash and all below a rule-based baseline; EcoGym needs 5 runs in Vending; EnterpriseBench best method flips between DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4.1; Can-LLMs-Be-CEOs used one run per scenario. Single-run rankings are unreliable.
agent_test: Evaluate any plan-vs-react scaffold with at least 3 runs per setting and 2 backbones; report mean and worst run.

claim: LLM strategic advice has a fashion bias (trendslop): preference for differentiation, augmentation and long-term options regardless of context; prompt and context fixes help little in the HBR study, but a pilot with GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (240 runs) finds model-specific behaviour (GPT-4o flips with specific context 72% to 98%; Claude resists adversarial instruction 75.0% vs 27.5%). HBR original not opened.
agent_test: Add a forced counter-case and a forced choice before strategy-like recommendations; test per model.

claim: A plan that records predicted observations and rewrites itself only on mismatch (AdaPlanner: ALFWorld 91.79%, MiniWoB++ 91.11%) is a working form of diffing intended against realised action. No study compares replan-every-step, on-failure and on-surprise at equal tokens, and none tests an explicit plan-vs-trace diff on long-horizon score.
agent_test: Run three arms at equal tokens: replan every step, on failure, on prediction mismatch; log plan-trace divergence rate.
